subject: MAP: Acme Health POC environment & close timeline
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: Acme Health POC environment & close timeline

Hi Elena —

Following our kickoff, I sketched a concise MAP focusing on the POC environment items we agreed are blocking sign-off: API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, and VPC peering. See the proposed cadence below and a couple of asks so we can lock dates. I attached a short MAP-draft.pdf for the mutual-action plan (high level).

1) Org & API access (May 11–14)
   - Redwood creates an org entry for Acme Health and issues temp eval API keys (14-day) tied to a service account.
   - Ask: please confirm the primary Org admin email and preferred subdomain (e.g., acme-prod or acme-staging).

2) Network & security (May 12–18)
   - Acme provides IP ranges to allowlist and networking contact for peering.
   - Redwood begins VPC peering request (we can do shared peering or cross-account; see options below).
   - Ask: send the CIDR list and indicate whether you need private connectivity or NAT egress only.

3) Smoke tests & acceptance (May 19–21)
   - Run a 48-hour smoke window: basic generation latency, auth flows, and data isolation checks.

4) Close & pilot handoff (target May 28)
   - Assuming successful smoke tests, we will finalize access, issue permanent API credentials, and transition to the pilot cadence.

Network options (high-level):
- Option A: VPC peering (private, lower latency) — exchange CIDRs, create peering, route propagation.
- Option B: IP allowlist + NAT egress (simpler, no peering) — whitelist Redwood egress IPs, use service accounts.

Attachments: MAP-draft.pdf (high-level tasks + owners).

Quick asks to keep the timeline:
- Reply with networking contact (name + email) and CIDR list by EOD Tue 5/11.
- Confirm the org admin email for Redwood to provision the eval keys.

Happy to hop on a 30-min technical sync tomorrow if needed — I can loop in Karthik and Marissa.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Elena — great, thanks for the fast turnaround. A few operational notes from my side to make provisioning frictionless:

- API keys & KMS: We support issuing eval keys that are KMS-bound. For customer-managed keys (CMK/HSM), we can integrate but it adds a small onboarding window (typically 1–2 business days to verify policies). If you want CMK for the permanent keys, we can provision temp eval keys first (KMS-wrapped by Redwood) and then rotate to your CMK at handoff.

- Temporary eval creds: I'll prepare a named service-account key tied to acme-poc-2026 and notify you when it's ready. Eval keys will default to 14-day validity unless you request a longer demo window.

- Network coordination: Tessa will own the VPC peering ticket from our side and coordinate IP exchange with Rajiv. Tessa, can you open the internal peering ticket and include the acme_net_list.csv?

- I've attached an operational checklist (acme-map-checklist.xlsx) mapping owners, SLAs, and minimal acceptance criteria for the smoke window.

If the 11am PT sync works, I'll join and bring the runbook so we can confirm steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Elena / team —

Thanks for the CIDR list. A few technical specifics to make the peering request and firewall changes precise:

- Redwood egress IPs (for the POC): 35.210.18.0/24, 34.82.10.0/24 (we'll provide a signed manifest in the peering ticket).
- Required outbound ports: 443 (TLS), 5228 (if you need push notifications), and 3478/19302 if you intend to use any STUN/TURN for browser workloads.
- CIDR exchange: Acme should provide a non-overlapping /24 or larger block for the peering. If you cannot provide dedicated CIDRs, we can use NAT + allowlist but that will limit inbound private connections.

Sample peering request snippet you can paste into your ticketing system:

"Peering request: Redwood Inference (project: redwood-poc) -> Acme Health (project: acme-net). Requested cross-account peering route: exchange CIDRs 10.40.0.0/24 (Acme) <-> 10.50.0.0/24 (Redwood). Enable route propagation and add two static routes for 10.50.0.0/24 via peering. Allow inbound TCP 443 from Redwood egress blocks."

HubSpot: Jordan / Marissa — I'm updating DEAL-2389 with the MAP milestones and will include acceptance checklist items from Marissa's spreadsheet. Elena, I'll drop the HubSpot link in the sync notes after this thread.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
